class: Any test that adapts recorded real-world data to its own fixture ids by string surgery on a product-built identifier (an order tag, a key, a code) re-implements the product's builder; when the builder's format changes, every such test on every branch built before the change breaks at once, and each branch's CI finds it separately.
mechanism: Tests re-tagged recorded Kite orders with `row['tag'].replace('OFS9V', f'OFS{sid}V')` and compared against hand-typed old-grammar tags, while the product's make_tag moved to the 8-character Q grammar (main #438); the tests then looked up `make_tag(sid, 1, 0)` among rows still tagged OFS and found none.

first_seen.evidence: CI run 39535119675: 2 failed, 2926 passed - `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)` at test_route_reconciliation_db.py:69

fix: Per instance: #478 3bbf99e (`_retag` via parse_tag -> make_tag), #452 ee89aa5 (plans take the tag Zerodha echoed; Q-tagged plans proven to close from the same replies, neither grammar picks up the other's rows). Store code was proven correct for both grammars (exact stored-tag match). Mechanism planned: tracker row RETAG-HELPER - one shared test helper that re-tags recorded replies through the product's parse_tag/make_tag, and a repo_scan test refusing string replace on a tag value in tests (detector as second layer, run-discipline C8).

detection.note: CI catches each instance only after a branch merges the format change. Sweep 2026-10-21 (git grep 'replace("OFS|f"OFS{' over 11 held branches): gc6/380-3 17 hits incl. the same `.replace("OFS9V", ...)` at test_route_reconciliation_db.py:53 (predates #438, basket.py:94 still builds OFS); gc6/orders-screen 11 (predates #438); gc6/net-roundtrip 3 extra in test_reconcile_attribution.py:84,95,500; the other 8 branches only main's 8 deliberate legacy-tag tests.

occurrences.evidence: 8 api tests red, run 39535305016 (`the trades of 'OFS70V1L0' sum to 0 units`; `{'Q0001010': ...} == {'OFS1V1L0': ...}`); fixed ee89aa5, test-only
